title: Qué darle de comer a un cachorro : guía semana a semana
summary: Aprende qué comer debe un cachorro según su edad. Guía práctica con porciones, frecuencia y los mejores alimentos para cachorros en Colombia.
body_text: Traer un cachorro a casa es uno de los momentos más emocionantes para cualquier petlover colombiano. Pero junto con la alegría llega la primera gran duda: ¿qué le doy de comer? ¿Cuánto? ¿Cada cuánto? La alimentación en los primeros meses de vida de un perro es la base de todo lo que vendrá después — su tamaño, su salud, su sistema inmune y hasta su temperamento. La buena noticia: no necesitas ser veterinario para alimentar bien a tu cachorro. Necesitas información clara y constancia. Esta guía te lleva por cada etapa, semana a semana, para que nunca tengas que adivinar. Dato importante Los primeros 12 meses son la etapa de crecimiento más acelerada en la vida de un perro. En este tiempo, un cachorro de raza mediana puede aumentar hasta 40 veces su peso de nacimiento. Cada comida cuenta. Las primeras 8 semanas: leche materna es insustituible Durante las primeras 8 semanas de vida, el alimento ideal para un cachorro es la leche de su madre. No hay ningún sustituto que iguale su composición: anticuerpos, nutrientes en las proporciones perfectas y factores de crecimiento que no se pueden replicar artificialmente. Si el cachorro está con su madre, no necesitas hacer nada más en términos de alimentación. Si por alguna razón el cachorro quedó huérfano o fue separado antes de las 8 semanas (algo que idealmente no debería ocurrir), necesitarás un sustituto de leche específico para cachorros. Jamás uses leche de vaca — los cachorros son intolerantes a la lactosa y puede causarles diarrea severa y deshidratación. ¿Puedo usar leche en polvo para bebés humanos? No. La composición de la leche humana es completamente diferente a la leche canina. Los sustitutos de leche para cachorros están formulados para replicar la composición específica de la leche de perra, con las proporciones correctas de proteína, grasa y carbohidratos. Encuéntralos en tiendas especializadas como LAIKA . De 2 a 4 meses: la transición al alimento sólido Semanas 8–10 · Primera transición Empezando con lo sólido A partir de las 8 semanas, el cachorro ya puede empezar a comer alimento sólido para cachorros. La transición debe ser gradual: empieza remojando las croquetas con agua tibia hasta obtener una papilla suave. Con el paso de los días, ve reduciendo el agua hasta servir las croquetas secas. Usa siempre alimento específico para cachorros — nunca el de adultos Las croquetas pequeñas facilitan la masticación en cachorros pequeños Ofrece agua fresca y limpia en todo momento, separada del plato de comida Frecuencia: 4 comidas al día en porciones pequeñas Meses 2–4 · Crecimiento acelerado La etapa de mayor demanda nutricional Entre los 2 y 4 meses, el cachorro está creciendo a una velocidad que nunca volverá a tener. Su demanda de proteína, grasa, calcio y fósforo está en su punto más alto. Sigue con 3 a 4 comidas al día, ajustando la cantidad según el peso y las indicaciones del empaque. Proteína mínima: 28% en base seca Grasa mínima: 17% en base seca Busca DHA (ácido docosahexaenoico) para el desarrollo cerebral Para razas grandes: elige fórmulas específicas con calcio/fósforo controlado De 4 a 6 meses: porciones y horario A partir de los 4 meses, la mayoría de los cachorros ya tienen sus dientes de leche completos y comen croquetas sin necesidad de remojarlas. Es el momento de establecer un horario fijo de alimentación: 3 comidas al día, distribuidas uniformemente (por ejemplo, 7am, 1pm y 7pm). Para calcular la porción, el mejor punto de partida son las indicaciones del empaque del alimento, basadas en el peso actual del cachorro. Pero recuerda que esas guías son estimados — cada perro es diferente. Si tu cachorro deja comida en el plato consistentemente, la porción está siendo demasiado grande. Si termina en segundos y parece buscar más, puede necesitar un poco más. El test de las costillas Pasa los dedos sobre las costillas de tu cachorro sin apretar. Deberías sentirlas fácilmente pero no verlas a simple vista. Si no las sientes en absoluto, está con sobrepeso. Si se ven marcadas, necesita más alimento. Este chequeo rápido funciona en todas las etapas de la vida. De 6 a 12 meses: el último tramo del crecimiento Meses 6–12 · Transición a adulto Reduciendo frecuencia, ajustando cantidad Entre los 6 y 12 meses puedes reducir a 2 comidas al día, siempre a horas fijas. El cachorro sigue siendo cachorro nutricionalmente — no pases al alimento de adulto todavía. Las razas pequeñas maduran antes (12 meses), mientras que las razas grandes pueden seguir como cachorros hasta los 18–24 meses. Razas pequeñas (menos de 10 kg adulto): cambia a alimento adulto al año Razas medianas (10–25 kg adulto): cambia a alimento adulto al año Razas grandes (más de 25 kg adulto): mantén alimento cachorro hasta los 18 meses Razas gigantes (más de 45 kg adulto): hasta los 24 meses como cachorro Alimentos que JAMÁS debes darle a tu cachorro Colombia tiene una cultura de compartir la comida del plato propio con los perros — el arroz, el hueso del pollo del sancocho, la fruta que sobró. Algunos de estos alimentos son inofensivos; otros pueden ser mortales para tu cachorro. Esto es lo que debes evitar siempre: Alimentos peligrosos para tu cachorro Chocolate y cacao (tóxico), uvas y pasas (daño renal), cebolla y ajo (anemia hemolítica), macadamia (toxicidad neurológica), xilitol — el endulzante en chicles y productos "sin azúcar" (hipoglucemia severa), aguacate (daño cardíaco en dosis altas), alcohol (incluso en cantidades mínimas), huesos cocinados (pueden astillarse y perforar el intestino). Si tu cachorro ingirió algo de esta lista, llama a tu veterinario inmediatamente. Hidratación: el nutriente que más se olvida El agua es el nutriente más importante para cualquier ser vivo, incluido tu cachorro. Un cachorro que come croquetas secas necesita acceso constante a agua fresca y limpia. Cambia el agua al menos dos veces al día y lava el bebedero con frecuencia — las bacterias se acumulan rápidamente, especialmente en el calor bogotano o en climas cálidos como los de Cali o Medellín. Los cachorros que comen alimento húmedo o cocido consumen más agua a través del alimento, pero igualmente deben tener agua disponible siempre. Si tu cachorro no toma agua, puede ser señal de una enfermedad o de que el agua no está lo suficientemente fresca. Algunos cachorros prefieren el agua corriente — considera una fuente de agua para mascotas si ves que no bebe suficiente. title: The SME opportunity: How banks can transform real-time payments into revenue
summary: Learn how banks can generate new revenue from real-time payments by targeting small- to medium-size enterprises (SMEs).
body_text: The rollout of real-time payments is progressing rapidly, benefiting consumers and the economy. However, the anticipated proliferation of new value-added services related to real-time payments has been slower than expected. Why is this, and what can we do about it? It’s clear that real-time payments will continue to replace traditional payments in most of the world's major economic markets. In the U.S., FedNow continues to grow in both volume and value, with more banks now able to send and receive real-time payments. In Europe, real-time Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA) payments will be mandatory by the end of this year. Further, the U.K.’s New Payments Architecture (NPA) is real-time focused. However, while the move to real-time payments continues, we haven’t seen the proliferation of new spin-off open banking services that were expected, as well as related new revenue streams and cost savings. Beyond immediate retail payments The value of immediate payments in terms of payment speed are self-evident across the entire value chain. However, the benefits immediate payments can deliver through value-added open banking services and, indeed, through ISO 20022 extend beyond the initial payment transaction and its speed. Open banking services, which sit on real-time payment rails such as Request to Pay (RTP) and Variable Recurring Payments (VRPs) , have been available in some markets (Europe) for a while but have yet to be widely adopted and still have a limited set of use cases. A possible reason for this might be the focus of regulators on the individual retail customer experience, with a less visible focus on small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and the commercial banking sector. As a result, the SME sector is relatively untouched by open banking services, creating opportunities for banks to use their investment in real-time payments and existing open banking developments to bring additional value to their SME customers. Thoughts on value While open banking services based on various real-time payment schemes often focus on the retail consumer, open banking also creates opportunities to deliver new and enhanced services for the SME market. Developments such as the increase (or removal) of upper-value limits in real-time payment schemes further enhance these opportunities. There are many SME value-creating services to consider. Of course, it’s now possible for banks to settle with their SME customers and make B2B payments using instant payments, with resulting improvements in cash flow. However, this is just the start. Banks can offer services such as RTP to SME customers as managed services (possibly embedded in an existing application), which provides SMEs a cheaper alternative to receiving payments by card. It can be said that card payments aren’t particularly built for SMEs; the fees are high compared to the transaction cost, and SMEs often have low transaction volumes. However, RTP provides a sensible alternative. Although an SME may be wary of adoption costs and risks, the bank could alleviate both by providing a prepackaged service. In addition, in Europe, VRPs offer a more flexible alternative to SEPA Direct Debit , with immediate settlement to the SME merchant and lower fees. This is just one additional example of a ready-to-use value-added service. Finally, the icing on this cake is the richer data in ISO 20022, which has the potential to improve reconciliation and provide greater market insights from payments data (especially over the limited data available from card schemes). Banks can play a significant role in helping their SME customers access the value of this data. Potential issues There are some considerations that need to be addressed. Some of these are in the bank’s control, with others less so. Ensuring that the bank’s real-time payment rail can support new value-added services is within the bank’s control and may be addressed in numerous ways. This might mean that real-time payments (SEPA Instant Credit Transfer/FedNow/Faster Payments/G3) are implemented in a different way within the bank, compared to other payment rails (perhaps, for example, as managed services where other rails are in-house). Further, banks that issue cards need to consider how RTP usage fits in with their card business. It wouldn’t make commercial sense to introduce new services to the detriment of an existing business; however, RTP has a role in displacing cash, driving up volumes and ensuring future SME markets. Finally, there is the practical consideration of integration with corporate enterprise resource planning (ERP) and treasury management systems, many of which aren’t yet operating in real-time payments. Advantages of a real-time payments platform Embracing a flexible, modern real-time payments platform offers significant opportunities beyond compliance. It can serve as a launchpad for a range of value-generating services. Such a platform combined with a real-time payment rail can simplify processes and provide an innovation path outside existing legacy infrastructure. It can take real-time payments to the next level, driving both new value-add services and market expansion. At CGI, we are having conversations with our clients about real-time payment and open banking solutions. If you’re interested in simplifying your payments journey and refining your strategy, please get in touch .

title: Why a Teaching Philosophy Matters
summary: How writing down your teaching philosophy can help you through your job search and beyond.
body_text: ‍ If you do an internet search for “teaching philosophy,” you’ll find dozens of samples, step-by-step guides, and formatted templates. But the reason for writing one isn’t to create a polished paragraph you can paste into your resume or frame on your classroom wall. Your teaching philosophy should be your North Star: a motivator and a reminder of why you teach. Why bother writing it down? There’s plenty of research showing that writing things down helps us remember them. As a job candidate, having your philosophy in writing keeps it fresh in your mind so that, when you’re asked about your beliefs—even in a stressful interview—you can answer with confidence. Instead of scrambling, you’ll draw on ideas you’ve already worked through: how you build relationships, how you manage your classroom, how you measure success. Writing your philosophy also forces you to clarify what matters most. When an interviewer asks why you teach or what motivates you, you won’t need to fall back on a cliché. You’ll have language that captures your values, your personal connection to the profession, and the difference you hope to make. Another benefit: your philosophy provides source material that ties your resume, cover letter, and interview responses together. By drawing from a well-articulated statement, you’ll demonstrate consistency across the hiring process, show that your passion is genuine, and give principals a clear sense of how you’ll contribute to their school. A compass, not a map A teaching philosophy isn’t meant to spell out every detail of how you’ll teach every subject. Instead, think of it as a compass: a set of guiding ideas that help you stay oriented even when circumstances change. Your philosophy should highlight what you believe students gain from having you as a teacher, and the ways you lead, engage, assess, and instruct to support positive outcomes. To help identify the direction you want your teaching to take, ask yourself: What makes me feel most proud as a teacher? How do I want my students to remember me? How do I intend to create the conditions for learning in my classroom? When you’re ready to start writing, consider using a guide like the one from the Center for Educational Innovation at the University of Minnesota , that comes from a research-backed institution with expertise in teaching and learning. More than words on paper The most important thing about your teaching philosophy is that it’s yours. It shouldn’t be a string of buzzwords or the phrases you think a hiring committee wants to hear. The value of your teaching philosophy comes from taking time to reflect and writing down what is true for you. If your written philosophy focuses on student-centered, inquiry-based learning but your actual practice is lectures and direct control, you will be perceived as inauthentic. Likewise, if you truly thrive with structure but your statement suggests you give students total autonomy, you will struggle to find a school that is a good fit for you. Your philosophy also matters once you’re in the classroom. When teaching gets tough (and it will), revisiting your core beliefs can help you refocus and keep going. Right now, as you explore schools, your philosophy can be a tool for comparison: does their mission line up with your beliefs? If so, you’re more likely to land somewhere you can truly thrive. In the end, knowing what matters to you and finding a school that aligns with that is what’s best for students, and best for you.

title: Best AI Tax Software for Tax Professionals in 2026
summary: Compare the best AI tax software for tax professionals in 2026 — AI tax research, writing, return review, preparation, planning, and client intelligence.
body_text: AI is reshaping the tax profession fast, but in 2026 the bar is higher than it was a year ago. The best AI tax software for tax professionals no longer just answers questions the way it did a year ago; it spans defensible tax research, return review, tax preparation, planning, and advisory work in a single platform, with citations a professional can stand behind . That matters because "AI tax software" has become a crowded label. It now spans everything from purpose-built tax systems to general-purpose AI tools adapted for tax , and that range is what determines whether a tool genuinely saves your firm hours or quietly adds review risk. This guide compares the leading AI tax platforms for tax professionals, what each does well, where each stops, and how they stack up side by side. Effective AI tax software has to go beyond simple automation. At a minimum, it should: Analyze complex issues and scenarios Interpret authoritative guidance and cite primary sources Retain client context across engagements Support decision-making across research, planning, preparation, and advisory workflows We group the tools below into two categories so you can match them to the work you actually do. AI tax software is built for professional tax research, reasoning, and practice-wide workflows, the focus of this guide. Sales tax automation tools (covered briefly toward the end) handle indirect-tax compliance such as sales tax, VAT, and GST; they're valuable in their lane but aren't designed to replace AI-driven research or decision support. These tools reflect a shift toward AI-driven tax research, reasoning, and workflow support, helping CPAs spend less time searching for answers and more time applying their expertise. Best AI Tax Software Tools in 2026 TaxGPT TaxGPT , the AI tax assistant trusted by 80,000+ active users, including CPAs, enrolled agents, tax attorneys, and preparers — is the complete AI Operating System purpose-built for tax, accounting, and advisory firms. Users have asked over 650,000 tax questions through the platform, with a 95% satisfaction rate. Built on proprietary AI models trained on thousands of authoritative sources vetted by CPAs and tax attorneys, TaxGPT unifies tax research, Client Intelligence, return reviews, return preparation, and autonomous agentic workflows — helping professionals interpret tax guidance, evaluate outcomes, and apply insights across the full range of tax scenarios. Whether you're a sole practitioner, a growing firm, or a multi-partner practice, TaxGPT helps you scale advisory work without sacrificing accuracy or professional judgment. For tax professionals and accounting firms, TaxGPT offers AI Tax Co-Pilot — a dedicated AI copilot for professional tax workflows. Tax Co-Pilot brings together TaxGPT's research, writing, review, and Client Intelligence capabilities into one unified workspace built around how tax professionals actually work: research a question, draft the memo, review the return, manage the client, all within a single platform that remembers your clients and learns from every interaction. ‍ Core TaxGPT Capabilities Tax Research TaxGPT AI tax research enables users to ask complex tax questions and receive structured, source-backed responses grounded in authoritative tax guidance, including the IRS, IRC, CRA, Treasury Regulations, court cases, and administrative rulings. Coverage spans U.S. federal, state, local, territorial, and treaty jurisdictions alongside Canadian federal and provincial tax law — helping reduce manual search time while supporting defensible tax positions across the full scope of tax topics. For client-specific situations, upload returns, financial statements, IRS/CRA notices, supporting schedules, or trial balances directly into your research session . TaxGPT analyzes documents in context, combining document-specific details with verified tax guidance to deliver personalized, defensible answers — without switching tools or losing your research thread. Tax Writer TaxGPT AI tax writer turns research into polished deliverables without starting from a blank page. TaxGPT Writer drafts client emails, tax memos, IRS and CRA notice responses, engagement letters, opinion letters, and white papers — all tailored to your firm's voice and your client's specific situation. This enables tax professionals to translate research and analysis into clear, client-ready deliverables in minutes rather than hours. Tax Matrix - Multi Jurisdiction Tax Research Allows professionals to compare tax implications across multiple states or jurisdictions side by side . Unlike static “state charts,” this is especially useful for evaluating multistate scenarios, like nexus threshold comparison for multiple states and understanding how differing rules affect outcomes. Client Intelligence An AI-powered client dashboard that serves as the contextual memory of your practice. It connects every client's tax history, entity structure, prior-year filings, and ongoing research threads into one intelligent profile, so every research output and written deliverable is personalized rather than generic. Client Intelligence strengthens its understanding with every interaction, evolving into a true intelligence layer that remembers context and continually improves the accuracy of your tax guidance. Agent Andrew Agent Andrew is an AI tax return reviewer that automates up to 90% of the tax return review process. By analyzing uploaded returns and source documents, Agent Andrew identifies potential errors, audit risks, and missed savings opportunities before filing. Issues are flagged using three color-coded categories: Red flags: audit risks, transcription errors, omissions, and compliance issues that reconcile returns to source documents. Green flags: missed tax savings such as home office deductions, retirement contributions, and depreciation elections. Cleared flags: resolved or rejected items that require no further action. Agent Andrew currently supports Forms 1040, 1065, 1120, and 1120-S, generating a detailed, downloadable report with actionable insights. TaxGPT Cowork – Agentic Workflow Platform TaxGPT Cowork is an agentic workflow platform built for tax, accounting, and advisory firms. It assigns dedicated AI agents to run the firm's most time-consuming workflows autonomously end to end, pulling documents from connected storage, operating inside existing tax and accounting software, and handing off to your team only when a judgment call is needed. Cowork covers the full workflow spectrum: AI Tax Preparation (1040, 1065, 1120, 1120 consolidated, and 1120-S — inside your existing tax software), Bookkeeping, Tax Planning, R&D Tax Credit Analysis, K-1 Production, Amended Returns, Extension Filing, Entity Structure Reviews, Tax Saving Opportunity Scans, and Interactive Tax Projection Models. Every workflow surfaces a full audit trail and keeps licensed professionals in the review seat, not the execution seat. Together, these capabilities position TaxGPT as the AI Operating System for tax, supporting professionals well beyond isolated tasks. By combining research, document intelligence, multi-jurisdiction analysis, return review, return preparation, and autonomous agentic workflows into a single AI-first system, TaxGPT helps users work more efficiently, stay organized, and deliver greater value to their clients without needing to stitch together multiple point solutions. Its research-first approach makes it a strong option for professionals who want focused support when navigating specific tax issues and interpreting guidance. Blue J is primarily designed for question-based tax research and does not extend into broader firm workflows such as return review, return preparation, and persistent client management. Read all about our in depth comparison between TaxGPT and Blue J here . CCH AnswerConnect CCH AnswerConnect is a well-established tax platform with strong tax and accounting research capabilities, making it a familiar and trusted option for many CPA firms. Its research functionality aligns closely with traditional tax research workflows, and as AI adoption expands across the industry, CCH AnswerConnect has introduced embedded AI features to help users surface answers and guidance within its broader tax and firm management ecosystem. For firms already in the Wolters Kluwer ecosystem, CCH AnswerConnect now pairs its editorial library with generative AI. The difference is that it is general-purpose AI applied to a research library, rather than a tax-purpose-built system that spans research, review, preparation, and advisory in one platform. Read all about our in depth comparison between TaxGPT and CCH AnswerConnect here . Filed Filed is an AI-powered tax preparation platform focused on automating return preparation. It extracts data from client documents and populates returns directly inside existing tax software, with a built-in reviewer that cross-checks the completed return against source documents. That makes it a practical option for firms looking to automate preparation. Filed has also introduced AI-driven features such as its AI Tax Advisor and AI Reviewer, which are designed to provide source-backed guidance and review returns for potential issues prior to filing. These tools extend Filed’s preparation-focused approach, though they remain centered on return-level workflows. In contrast, TaxGPT takes a broader AI-first approach by focusing on the following: AI Tax Preparation for 1040, 1065, 1120, 1120 consolidated, and 1120-S returns — inside your existing tax software Tax research grounded in IRS, IRC, CRA, Treasury Regulations, and court cases Multi-jurisdiction analysis across federal, state, provincial, and treaty law Client communications , including IRS/CRA notice responses Client Intelligence that retains tax history and entity context across engagements Advisory and planning workflows including R&D credit, entity structure review, and tax projections Thus enabling users to move beyond just preparation and apply AI across a wider range of professional use cases. Bizora Bizora is an AI-native tax research platform built around citation transparency. Instead of keyword search, users ask questions in plain English and receive answers linked directly to the IRC, Treasury Regulations, IRS rulings, and case law. Its feature, “View Steps,” exposes the full reasoning path behind an answer, useful for documentation and internal review. Bizora also offers integrated memo and email drafting (Canvas), a document workspace with AI analysis (the Vault), all-50-state coverage including property and sales tax research. That research-first design also marks its boundary. Bizora concentrates on research and the deliverables that flow from it, rather than autonomous return preparation, agentic workflows, or return review at scale. For firms that want one platform spanning research, preparation, review, and advisory, that is where TaxGPT’s broader scope applies. Hive Tax Hive Tax is an AI platform aimed at small CPA firms, combining tax research, planning, return analysis, and client support in one tool. Its research returns cited answers drawn from primary federal and state sources and tax court cases; its planning assistant builds strategies around goals like liability reduction and retirement optimization; and its return-analysis feature flags discrepancies and overlooked deductions and credits. Hive is purpose-built for the needs of smaller practices, which is both its strength and its scope. Its planning depth and feature breadth are lighter than a full firm-wide operating system, and it does not offer autonomous agentic workflows or return preparation inside existing tax software. It is a strong fit for boutique firms; growing and multi-partner practices that need research, preparation, review, Client Intelligence, and agentic workflows in one system are the case for TaxGPT.

title: More than Block Storage: Three Ways Everpure Connects Your Nutanix Infrastructure
summary: Everpure extends Nutanix infrastructure beyond block storage with shared file, object, and Kubernetes-native data management for enterprise workloads.
body_text: Summary Everpure enhances Nutanix infrastructure beyond block storage by delivering unified file, object, and Kubernetes-native data management for modern enterprise workloads. In late 2025, the integrated solution combining Nutanix Cloud Platform (NCP) and Everpure™ FlashArray ™ became generally available. The solution deeply integrates FlashArray storage functionality into the core of the Nutanix platform. Storage functionality is fully offloaded (volumes, snapshots, cloning, etc.), but entirely managed within Nutanix Prism, giving users the value of Purity software and the same day-to-day management experience Nutanix users are used to. This is not just a simple integration. It’s a true co-engineering of the platforms into a seamless stack, preserving the look, feel, and experience of HCI, but with the value proposition of external storage. This solution has had an interesting side effect: People have assumed they can’t use any storage with Nutanix unless it’s deeply integrated into the Nutanix stack. While this is certainly the best path for day-to-day block storage management for your VMs, it is not the only path, and block is not the only way to consume storage. For many use cases, it isn’t even the preferred path. Data is consumed in different ways at different layers of a technology stack. File, object, and block all have different use cases and methods for control. Increasingly, storage consumption is heavily being driven at the application layer where the need to store and access massive unstructured data sets has become the primary driver for storage growth. These range from traditional use cases such as shared content repositories or user space to modern initiatives like AI inferencing or Kubernetes-deployed apps. The key point is that while most, if not all, of your infrastructure is running on VMs, the virtualized infrastructure is not the only touchpoint to your storage. That’s where the Enterprise Data Cloud (EDC) becomes strategic. The combined Unified Data Plane that is made up of FlashArray , FlashBlade ®, Everpure Cloud , and Portworx ® attacks these data problems from all vectors. The EDC can provide consistent enterprise storage services across Nutanix HCI clusters, disaggregated compute deployments, Nutanix Cloud Cluster (NC2) environments, Kubernetes platforms, and AI infrastructure. Let’s dig into the many ways that our Unified Data Plane combines with the Nutanix Cloud Platform to solve all storage needs. Shared file and object storage across Nutanix environments Not every workload needs block storage, and increasingly, much of the most important data does not belong to a single virtual machine at all. One or more VMs and their apps are consumers of that data, not exclusive owners. AI data sets, VDI user shares, backup repositories, home directories, analytics pipelines, legal documents, media libraries, archive data, and shared application content all live in the world of files and objects. None of these things generally exist on a traditional virtual disk. Everpure FlashArray and FlashBlade can provide these services directly to workloads running across Nutanix environments, including Nutanix HCI clusters and Nutanix compute-only nodes. Because the access method is native file or object storage over the network, virtual machine operating systems and/or their hosted applications can directly consume NFS exports, SMB shares, or S3 buckets without requiring direct Nutanix storage integration. That makes the same data set available to workloads running in different places without forcing the data to be copied, replicated, or tied to a single Nutanix cluster. This is also not limited to a single protocol or a single use case at a time. In many environments, these workflows run in parallel. A single Everpure storage platform can support SMB shares for user data, NFS exports for application and analytics workloads, and access to S3 buckets at the same time. That matters because unstructured data rarely fits neatly into one access model. Home directories and VDI user shares are good examples. The virtual desktop may be non-persistent, but the user’s data is not. User shares and persistent user data can be centralized on FlashArray or FlashBlade file services and accessed by desktops or application servers running on Nutanix. This gives the environment a common place to protect, replicate, and recover user data without tying it to an individual VM lifecycle. Figure 1: Basic file connectivity via SMB or NFS is available from both FlashArray and FlashBlade. AI and analytics are another natural fit. Platforms such as Nutanix AI depend on shared access to unstructured data, including data sets, model artifacts, and application content. FlashBlade is well-suited for high-performance unstructured data, while FlashArray file services can consolidate shared data and migration use cases that benefit from low latency and integration with the broader enterprise storage environment. Figure 2: Example of setting up a FlashArray S3 bucket to be used with Velero and Nutanix Kubernetes Platform. This is where shared file and object storage becomes more strategic than simply attaching a share to a virtual machine. It becomes a common data layer for workloads that need shared access across clusters. Since that data is often business-critical, it also needs enterprise protection features such as snapshots, replication, SafeMode™ Snapshots , and disaster recovery workflows. Kubernetes-native storage with Portworx PX-CSI for NKP Kubernetes introduces another storage consumption model. Instead of managing storage around individual virtual machines, applications request persistent storage through Kubernetes constructs such as StorageClasses, PersistentVolumes, PersistentVolumeClaims, and VolumeSnapshots. For Nutanix Kubernetes Platform (NKP) environments, Everpure PX-CSI provides another way to consume FlashArray and FlashBlade storage through Kubernetes-native workflows. This can be useful for teams that want Kubernetes storage automation to connect more directly with Everpure platforms while still operating inside the familiar Kubernetes control plane. Figure 3: Everpure FlashArray and FlashBlade StorageClasses listed on an NKP cluster. Nutanix AI is a good example of where this Kubernetes consumption model matters. The data layer may include file and object storage for AI data sets and model content, but the services running inside NKP still need persistent storage presented through Kubernetes-native workflows. PX-CSI gives platform teams another way to expose FlashArray and FlashBlade services to those applications while keeping storage consumption aligned with Kubernetes operations. There is also a native Nutanix CSI path. FlashArray can work with NKP using the Nutanix CSI driver for block storage through Nutanix volume groups, while FlashBlade can be used for NFS-based persistent storage. That remains a solid option for environments that want to consume storage through the NKP default StorageClass options. The key point is optionality. The Nutanix CSI driver provides a native Nutanix path, while PX-CSI gives another way to bring FlashArray and FlashBlade services into Kubernetes workflows when that’s the right fit. Direct VM-to-array connectivity with NVMe-oF/TCP and iSCSI The Prism-integrated method for FlashArray block storage is the Nutanix workflow getting the most attention, and for good reason. In that model, Nutanix manages the external storage connection and presents FlashArray-backed storage through familiar Prism workflows for virtual machine boot and data volumes. One approach worth exploring is using FlashArray//C ™ through the integrated path for VM boot volumes and general workloads, while those same VMs connect directly in-guest via NVMe-oF/TCP or iSCSI to a FlashArray//XL ™ system for applications and databases where the increased performance provided by direct storage access is critical. Figure 4: Example of Nutanix in-guest connectivity options. This option is useful for database platforms and workloads where storage connectivity needs to exist inside the guest rather than through the hypervisor. It’s also a key option for NC2 and HCI environments where hypervisor-level FlashArray connectivity is not yet available. In those deployments, in-guest connectivity via NVMe-oF/TCP or iSCSI becomes the primary path for VMs and applications that need to consume FlashArray storage directly, regardless of what the underlying hypervisor or cloud infrastructure supports. In this model, volumes are managed outside Prism, but they’re still able to utilize FlashArray data services, including data reduction, replication, protection groups, and SafeMode immutability. Clustered applications such as Microsoft WSFC can also be supported through FlashArray host groups containing the NQN or IQN identifiers for the participating VMs. This does not replace Prism-integrated FlashArray storage; the two approaches can coexist, with Prism-managed storage used for general VM workloads and guest-connected NVMe-oF/TCP or iSCSI reserved for specialized clustering requirements. FlashArray and FlashBlade as shared storage platforms The capabilities discussed here, including guest-connected block storage, shared file services, object storage, and PX-CSI, are all available today for Nutanix and Everpure customers, without requiring major architectural changes. More importantly, they complement standard Prism-integrated storage workflows instead of replacing them. Regardless of whether your Nutanix environment is built around HCI, disaggregated compute, NC2, Kubernetes, or some combination of them, Everpure can operate as more than just external block storage for a single cluster. It becomes a centralized enterprise storage platform spanning clusters, protocols, and workload types while delivering consistent storage services across the environment. These are the integration points worth exploring if the goal is to maximize the value of both Nutanix and Everpure working together. title: SAFE Conversion Scenarios Every Founder Should Understand
summary: Learn how SAFE conversion affects dilution across caps, discounts, MFNs, option pools, and pre- vs post-money SAFEs—plus how to model rounds and avoid surprises.
body_text: Why SAFE conversion deserves more attention than the SAFE itself A SAFE , short for Simple Agreement for Future Equity, feels simple on the day you sign it. Money comes in, legal costs stay relatively low, and you postpone a priced equity round. The hard part usually shows up later, when that SAFE converts and changes the ownership math. SAFE conversion is the point where a SAFE turns into actual shares, and it is an ownership event, not a formality. If your company has multiple SAFEs, an option pool, unvested stock, and a new lead investor asking for a larger pool before closing, small recordkeeping mistakes turn into material dilution surprises. Y Combinator introduced SAFEs in 2013, and they became widely adopted because they let startups raise capital without setting a valuation upfront, while still giving investors a contractual right to receive equity later . That trade-off is exactly why conversion deserves more planning than the SAFE itself ever gets. What is a SAFE conversion? SAFE conversion is the process by which a Simple Agreement for Future Equity turns into equity shares, typically triggered by the company’s next priced financing round. The SAFE holder does not own shares until conversion happens. Before that point, they hold a contractual right to receive equity later, priced according to the terms in the agreement: the valuation cap, the discount, and any most-favored nation (MFN) provision. What needs to be in place before a SAFE converts Clean ownership data comes first Before you model any conversion, gather the details for every security already on the cap table: Each SAFE investor, investment amount, signing date, valuation cap, and discount Any MFN provision Any side letter with pro rata or other special rights You also need accurate equity records outside the SAFEs themselves. Confirm the number of common shares outstanding, restricted stock awards, option grants, exercised options, canceled grants, and the current reserved option pool. If vesting schedules are wrong or stale, your fully diluted share count will be wrong too, and that can distort round modeling. This is why founders should treat the cap table as a living operating record, not a document they clean up only when financing counsel asks for it. A single source of truth matters most right before conversion, when every security starts interacting with every other security. SAFEs don’t exist in isolation A spreadsheet can work when there is one SAFE and a tiny team. It gets fragile once you add overlapping instruments and timing questions. A post-money SAFE, a pre-money SAFE, a pool expansion, and employee grants issued between fundraising steps can all affect final ownership. Founders who model those pieces together are better prepared for diligence and less likely to discover cap table issues a week before closing. How SAFE conversion actually works The terms that change the math Most SAFE conversions turn on a few core terms. Valuation cap sets the maximum company valuation used to calculate the SAFE holder’s conversion price. A lower cap usually means the investor receives shares at a lower effective price, which means more shares. Discount gives the investor a percentage reduction from the next round’s price per share. MFN (most-favored nation) can let an earlier SAFE holder adopt better economic terms from a later SAFE. Pre-money vs. post-money SAFEs . Post-money SAFEs make ownership easier to estimate because they are designed to define the investor’s ownership after that SAFE investment and before the new priced money arrives. Pre-money SAFEs can be less intuitive because the impact of later SAFEs and pool changes can shift the final dilution outcome, as described in Mantle’s SAFE guide . The usual triggers, and the less obvious ones The most common conversion trigger is the next priced equity financing. That is the scenario most founders expect. But SAFEs can also be affected by acquisitions, IPOs, and other liquidity events, depending on the contract. In those cases, the instrument may convert, cash out, or follow another contract-specific path. The important habit is to read the trigger language before you sign. The conversion scenarios that catch founders off guard High-valuation rounds can still create heavy dilution Founders often assume a strong priced round means old SAFEs will be less painful. Not necessarily. If the next round is priced well above a SAFE’s valuation cap, the SAFE usually converts at the cap, not at the higher round price. That can make the SAFE dramatically more dilutive than the founder expected. Down rounds change who bears the pain In a down round, the economics can shift again. Depending on the terms, the SAFE may still convert at more favorable economics than the new investor price, or the discount may become the better deal. You can’t judge the impact from the headline valuation alone. You have to test the actual conversion formulas. Multiple SAFEs stack, they do not average out Two SAFEs with the same dollar amount can produce very different outcomes if one has a $5 million cap and the other has a $10 million cap. Add MFN rights or a required option pool increase, and the stack becomes even more complex. That is why scenario modeling matters more than rough intuition. A simple worked example Assume the company has 8,000,000 fully diluted shares before the next round, plus 1,000,000 shares reserved in the option pool. It has two outstanding SAFEs: Instrument Amount invested Key term SAFE A $250,000 $5,000,000 valuation cap SAFE B $250,000 $10,000,000 valuation cap Now assume the next priced round is done at a $20,000,000 pre-money valuation. In that scenario, SAFE A is likely to convert using the $5,000,000 cap, because that is more favorable to the investor than the round price. SAFE B is likely to convert using the $10,000,000 cap. Even though both investors put in the same amount, SAFE A receives meaningfully more shares because its cap is lower. The founder takeaway isn’t the exact share count in the abstract. It’s that ownership depends on the full stack: existing common stock, all SAFEs, the option pool, and any pool top-up required by the new financing. If you want a more practical way to test those outcomes before a round, it helps to model dilution scenarios in advance . How to prepare for conversion without scrambling Ask Clerk before you model anything You don’t need to open five tabs to check where things stand. Drop your documents or just ask Mantle Clerk directly: which SAFEs are outstanding, what’s the current option pool, has anything changed since the last time you looked. Mantle Clerk encodes operational expertise, the mechanics, the timing, the “what happens if” reasoning that lives between formal legal questions. Legal questions still go to counsel, but the operational picture you need before a round is exactly what Clerk is built to answer. Let Clerk handle the closing paperwork When the round actually closes, this is normally the worst week of the process: SPAs, side letters, six different SAFE conversions, all needing manual entry. With Clerk, you hand over the documents and it does the reconciliation conversationally. “We just closed our seed. Here’s the signed SPA and closing binder.” “Nice work! I’ve found your updated charters with 2 new share classes, 7 new shareholders, 6 SAFE conversions, and an update to your equity plan. Let’s start with the share classes and work our way down.” Instead of reconstructing the cap table from a stack of PDFs, you’re confirming what Clerk already found, one item at a time. Run a tie-out before the term sheet Founders usually only discover a missing side letter during diligence, when it’s expensive to explain. Clerk runs tie-outs methodically and flags the gaps in a closing package that are easy to miss and expensive to explain. Ask it to do this before you’re deep in term sheet negotiations, so any gap gets fixed while it’s still just an email to an investor, not a diligence flag. Model the round, then ask Clerk to explain it Mantle’s Term Sheet Modeler does the heavy lifting on the math. Upload the term sheet and it shows exactly how the round hits your cap table and dilution. You don’t have to interpret the output alone. Ask Clerk directly: why is the low-cap SAFE converting to more shares than the high-cap one, or what does the pool top-up actually cost the founders. Hand off clean, on request Once conversion is final, you can instantly download your cap table spreadsheet to share with legal counsel, auditors, or the next round’s investors. What to look for in software that supports SAFE management Good equity software should do three things well. Maintain accurate records for SAFEs, options, and vesting in one place. Update the cap table automatically as those records change. Let you model financing scenarios before you commit to them. SAFE conversion isn’t a one-line formula. It is a coordinated cap table event. Teams that keep ownership records current, track vesting and grants continuously, and test conversion outcomes before the next financing closes are the ones who aren’t scrambling the week of the deal. FAQ: SAFE Conversion When does a SAFE convert to equity? Most SAFEs convert at the company’s next priced equity financing round. Some also convert, or follow a separate contract-specific path, in the event of an acquisition, IPO, or other liquidity event. Does a SAFE convert at the valuation cap or the round price? Most SAFEs convert at the company’s next priced equity financing round. Some also convert, or follow a separate contract-specific path, in the event of an acquisition, IPO, or other liquidity event. What happens to SAFEs in a down round? The economics can still favor the SAFE holder over new investors, depending on the cap and discount terms. A down round doesn’t automatically mean SAFE holders take less favorable pricing than the new money. Do multiple SAFEs convert at the same price? No. Each SAFE converts according to its own terms. Two SAFEs for the same amount can convert into very different share counts if they carry different valuation caps. What is the difference between a pre-money and post-money SAFE? A post-money SAFE fixes the investor’s ownership percentage immediately after that investment, before new priced-round money arrives. A pre-money SAFE’s final ownership impact depends on what else converts or gets added to the cap table before the round closes.
